black-pepper.definition: A pungent spice made from dried peppercorns of the Piper nigrum plant.
black-pepper.exampleUsage: Black pepper was ground over the soup.

paprika.definition: Plant bearing large mild thick-walled usually bell-shaped fruits.

cinnamon.definition: A sweet-smelling spice made from tree bark.

cumin.definition: Aromatic seeds of the cumin herb of the carrot family.

turmeric.definition: Ground dried rhizome of the turmeric plant used as seasoning.

chili-powder.definition: A powdered seasoning made from ground dried chili peppers, sometimes blended with other spices.
chili-powder.exampleUsage: The recipe used a small amount of chili powder.

nutmeg.definition: East Indian tree widely cultivated in the tropics for its aromatic seed.

clove.definition: Aromatic flower bud of a clove tree.

cardamom.definition: Aromatic seeds used as seasoning like cinnamon and cloves especially in pickles and barbecue sauces.

oregano.definition: An aromatic herb often used to season Mediterranean food.

thyme.definition: Any of various mints of the genus Thymus.

rosemary.definition: Widely cultivated for its fragrant grey-green leaves used in cooking and in perfumery.

parsley.definition: Annual or perennial herb with aromatic leaves.

cilantro.definition: Old World herb with aromatic leaves and seed resembling parsley.

dill.definition: Aromatic threadlike foliage of the dill plant used as seasoning.

mint.definition: A candy that is flavored with a mint oil.

bay-leaf.definition: A dried leaf from the bay laurel tree is used to season soups, stews, and sauces.

sage.definition: Of the grey-green color of sage leaves.

ketchup.definition: Thick spicy sauce made from tomatoes.

mustard.definition: Pungent powder or paste prepared from ground mustard seeds.

mayonnaise.definition: Egg yolks and oil and vinegar.

soy-sauce.definition: This dark, salty liquid is produced by fermenting soybeans, usually with wheat, salt, and water. It is used to add savory flavor and color to food, particularly in East Asian cuisines.

hot-sauce.definition: A strongly spicy sauce prepared from hot peppers and used to season food.

worcestershire.definition: A savory sauce of vinegar and soy sauce and spices.

barbecue-sauce.definition: A flavorful sauce, usually made from tomatoes, is used with grilled, smoked, or roasted meat. It may be brushed on during cooking, used as a marinade, or served at the table.

teriyaki.definition: Beef or chicken or seafood marinated in spicy soy sauce and grilled or broiled.

pesto.definition: A sauce typically served with pasta.

salsa.definition: Spicy sauce of tomatoes and onions and chili peppers to accompany Mexican foods.

olive-oil.definition: A liquid fat made by pressing or extracting oil from olives, olive oil is used mainly to prepare and eat food.

vegetable-oil.definition: Describes food ingredients that contain oil extracted from plants.

coconut-oil.definition: An edible oil extracted from coconut meat is used in cooking, baking, processed foods, cosmetics, and soap production.

sesame-oil.definition: A cooking oil produced by pressing or extracting oil from sesame seeds.

balsamic-vinegar.definition: A dark, sweet-tart vinegar traditionally associated with grape must and Italian production.
balsamic-vinegar.exampleUsage: Balsamic vinegar was used in the salad dressing.

red-wine-vinegar.definition: A vinegar produced from red wine after acetic fermentation, containing little or no alcohol in the finished culinary product.
red-wine-vinegar.exampleUsage: Red-wine vinegar added acidity to the dressing.

apple-cider-vinegar.definition: A vinegar made by fermenting apple cider into acetic acid.
apple-cider-vinegar.exampleUsage: Apple-cider vinegar has a sharp acidic flavor.

rice-vinegar.definition: A mild vinegar traditionally made from fermented rice or rice-derived alcohol.
rice-vinegar.exampleUsage: Rice vinegar was added to the salad dressing.

white-vinegar.definition: A clear strongly acidic vinegar commonly made from diluted acetic acid produced by fermentation.
white-vinegar.exampleUsage: White vinegar was listed among the pantry ingredients.

truffle-oil.definition: A flavored culinary oil made or scented to resemble the aroma of truffles.
truffle-oil.exampleUsage: A small amount of truffle oil flavored the finished dish.

maple-syrup.definition: A sweet syrup made by concentrating the sap of maple trees.
maple-syrup.exampleUsage: Maple syrup was served with pancakes.

jam.definition: A sweet spread made by cooking fruit with sugar.

jelly.definition: An edible jelly (sweet or pungent) made with gelatin and used as a dessert or salad base or a coating for foods.

peanut-butter.definition: A spread made mainly from ground roasted peanuts.
peanut-butter.exampleUsage: She spread peanut butter on toast.

nutella.definition: A brand of sweet hazelnut-and-cocoa spread.
nutella.exampleUsage: The jar contained a hazelnut cocoa spread.

marmalade.definition: A preserve made of the pulp and rind of citrus fruits.

molasses.definition: Thick dark syrup produced by boiling down juice from sugar cane.

agave.definition: Tropical American plants with basal rosettes of fibrous sword-shaped leaves and flowers in tall spikes.
